answer: A per-epoch sybil tax blocks bulk identity forgery: each live identity pays a recurring sunk cost. Each identity holds one kernel record binding its key to its tax account, shared by none. Each epoch the registry burns 30 credits per identity; a public pulse check lists payers, and missed payment zeroes weight. The k-th clone still pays 30, so 1,000 clones cost 30,000 per epoch with no bulk discount; tax farming fails because a quill-signed receipt covers one identity only, while an honest agent pays 30 once and keeps full weight.
